newsitem.title: UK: Heseltine implies Labour-BA sweetheart deal.
newsitem.headline: Heseltine implies Labour-BA sweetheart deal.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine implied on Tuesday that the Labour party would exempt British Airways Plc from its proposed windfall tax as a favour to the company's chief executive, Robert Ayling.
Labour confirmed at the weekend that Ayling was one of several leading businessmen who dined periodically with Blair and offered him advice in a personal capacity.
Speaking at a business conference that was also addressed by Blair, Heseltine noted that Labour had a clear political commitment to levy a windfall tax.
"We read that British Airways have escaped the net. I've heard that there is no such thing as a free lunch. Evidently, if you work at it, there can be free dinners," he said.
Quizzed by reporters later, Heseltine denied he was accusing British Airways of striking a sweetheart deal with Labour.
He said he was merely pointing out the inconsistencies of the proposed tax by repeating newspaper reports that British Airways had been excluded.
"If they're out, who's in?" he asked, adding that Labour had linked up in 1995 with British Telecommunications Plc to promise the creation of an information superhighway.
A Labour spokesman said the party had always said that the windfall tax would apply to the excess profits of privatised utilities operating in monopoly markets. "BA's not a utility," he added.
